title: Release sprint orchestration: RC sequencing, LTS gate policies, and annotated release-notes automation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Our weekly release cadence lacks an automated sequencing layer to produce stable RCs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private builds, align LTS demarcation rules, and generate annotated release notes tied to CI metadata. Manual steps create off-by-one errors in RC tagging, inconsistent LTS promotion windows, and missing context in release notes (missing regression links, dashboard snapshots, and rollout playbooks).

Goal: Ship a small "RC Sequencer" service and a Release Notes Pipeline to: 1) deterministically compute candidate RC tag sets per slice/sprint; 2) apply LTS eligibility & gating rules; 3) produce annotated, reviewer-friendly release notes (changelogs grouped by risk, associated PRs/commits, CI stability signals, and rollout instructions).

Out-of-scope: Full rollout automation (CD) and cross-region job scheduling for this ticket; those are follow-ups.

Success metrics: Reduce manual steps in cut process by 80%, eliminate off-by-one RC tag incidents, and reduce time-to-publish release notes from ~3 hours to <20 minutes after cut.
acceptance_criteria: RC Sequencer produces a JSON candidate RC manifest for each weekly slice and saves it to S3 with predictable path scheme.
LTS gate evaluator flags builds that meet LTS criteria (age of parent commit, regression-free window, security-fix tags) and adds LTS eligibility annotations.

Release Notes Pipeline assembles annotated notes including: grouped changelog by risk (major/medium/minor), links to GitHub PRs, CI job stability summary, top failing/regressing tests, and a generated rollout checklist.
Automation provides a preview URL (internal) for PM/Design/Eng reviewers and a one-click publish that tags the RC and pushes notes to the releases page.
All artifacts include traceable links to dashboards (Datadog/Grafana) and the central changelog blob for auditability.

notes: Design trade-off: store sequencer state in S3 blobs keyed by week vs. lightweight DB (Postgres). S3 chosen for immutability and ease of rollbacks; if we need complex queries later we'll add a small read replica indexer.
Tagging policy: RC tag format decided as 'rc/<YYYY>.<WEEK>.<SLICE>-<variant>' to avoid collisions with release branches. This diverges from earlier ad-hoc tags but was reviewed by infra and accepted.

LTS demarcation rules drafted with PM: build must be present on hosted for 4 weeks with <0.5% regression rate and must include explicit 'lts-candidate' label on at least one PR. Security fixes may expedite LTS via manual override.
Rollback plan: sequencer will mark 'publish-blocker' if any high-severity CI failures are detected; when publishing, tagging is done via signed pipeline and releases marked 'draft' until approval.
